role.altitude: The neuropsychologist keeps consulting colleagues, designing rehabilitation, supervising interns and learning; collecting test profiles and referral letters, typing consultation notes and plans, filling paper training forms and searching for accredited courses shrink.
skills_to_grow: Correcting speech-drafted notes quickly and completely
Checking drafted plans against the test findings
role.ambitious_version: A neuropsychologist whose notes and plans are drafted from what they said, so the hours go to patients and interns.

tasks.short: Find and select accredited courses, register and arrange time off, participate in educational programs, in-service training or workshops, and record accreditation points.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist finds and selects accredited courses that match their development needs
Neuropsychologist registers for the course and requests time off
Neuropsychologist attends and takes part in educational programs, in-service training or workshops
Course provider registers the attendance points in the accreditation portal
Neuropsychologist records accreditation points and certificates for re-registration

tasks.design: The professional body's accreditation portal lists courses with topic and points, and the neuropsychologist filters it by their development plan instead of collecting mailings. Registration and the time-off request go through the course page and the HR system. Course providers register attendance points in the same portal, so the neuropsychologist checks the running total for re-registration instead of keeping certificates in a folder. Choosing and taking part stay with the neuropsychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses came by mail and certificates were kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Accreditation portals where providers register attendance.
tasks.still_hard: Courses abroad that do not register points.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what will improve their practice, not what is easy to collect.
tasks.altitude: Less admin around courses; learning stays.

reach.learn: Whether development plans and courses line up.

evidence.claim: Professional bodies run accreditation portals where course providers register attendance points.

assumptions: Boundary: formal courses and training; reading literature and joining professional organizations (task 22205) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: providers register points (s3b, share 1, supplier) for about 80% of courses; the rest are uploaded by hand; s4 is priced at that share.
Taking part keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of courses whose providers register points.
research_questions: Is re-registration prepared with less effort?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist keeps their development plan current in the portal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many courses are outside the portal, so they are still found from mailings (s1 keeps 90) and points uploaded by hand (s4 keeps 60) (8.4); high: most courses with registered points (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the case from the record, consult with other professionals about patients' neurological conditions, record and sign the consultation note, and send it to the referring professional.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist gathers test results, scans and referral questions before the consultation
Neuropsychologist consults with other professionals about the patient's neurological condition and agrees next steps
Neuropsychologist records the consultation note

loop.input: The neuropsychologist's spoken summary after the consultation.
loop.output: A draft consultation note in the record's template: question, findings discussed, advice and next steps.
loop.check: Every finding must match a result in the record; the neuropsychologist reads each drafted statement against their spoken summary and the record and corrects the draft line by line.
loop.stop: The neuropsychologist signs the note, or types it by hand when the draft is poor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken summaries vary in order and wording.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist checks the final consultation note against the agreed advice and the record, signs it, and confirms the referring professional it goes to
Neuropsychologist sends the signed note to the referring professional by secure messaging

approvals.approved_version: The consultation note exactly as checked and signed by the neuropsychologist in s4, sent once by secure messaging to the referring professional named in the referral; any edit needs a new signature before sending.

tasks.design: A case overview in the patient record shows test results, scans and the referral question on one screen, so preparing means reading one page instead of searching. The consultation itself stays a conversation. Afterwards the neuropsychologist speaks a short summary, and a speech-to-note step drafts the note in the template; every finding must match a result in the record. The neuropsychologist corrects and signs the note, then sends that signed version by secure messaging. Only the neuropsychologist's summary is recorded, not the consultation, and the recording is deleted once the note is signed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after the consultation and results sat in several places.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-driven reporting in mental health care and record overviews.
tasks.still_hard: Complex cases where the advice is uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining what a test profile means for this patient's daily life.

reach.learn: Whether advice arrives sooner after a consultation.

evidence.claim: 24 of 25 large Dutch mental health providers use speech-driven reporting.
In a child mental health clinic median admin time per encounter fell from 27 to 10 minutes with ambient voice notes.
The psychologist stays accountable for AI-drafted notes.

assumptions: Boundary: consulting colleagues; writing neuropsychological reports (task 22206) and diagnosing and treating (task 22197) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: test results and scans stored in the patient record by the testing and radiology staff.

The consultation, signing and sending keep their full time; the clinic case was ambient notes of patient encounters, so a smaller cut is assumed for short spoken summaries: s3 keeps 70 because the neuropsychologist still composes the summary and corrects the draft.
unknowns: How many consultations are recorded as notes.
research_questions: Is the note time per consultation lower without more corrections later?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist reports systematic drafting errors to the application owner.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short notes needing many corrections (s3 keeps 90) and results not all in the record (s1 keeps 85) (4.5); high: longer notes drafted well (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare teaching material, educate and supervise practicum students, psychology interns or hospital staff, review interns' work, and complete and submit the interns' evaluations and supervision hours.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist prepares teaching material and anonymised case examples for supervision and staff training

loop.input: The neuropsychologist's outline and the department's protocols and test manuals.
loop.check: Every statement about a test or protocol must cite its manual or protocol section; case examples contain no patient identifiers; the neuropsychologist reads each slide against the cited section and corrects it.
loop.stop: The neuropsychologist keeps the material, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each group needs a different level and focus.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist educates and supervises practicum students, psychology interns and hospital staff in sessions
Neuropsychologist reviews interns' test administrations and reports and gives feedback
Intern logs supervision hours in the training institute's portal
Neuropsychologist writes the intern's competency evaluation
Neuropsychologist checks the final evaluation and the intern's hours log against the sessions held, and the training institute it goes to
Neuropsychologist submits the evaluation and confirms the hours to the training institute

approvals.approved_version: The evaluation text and the hours log exactly as checked by the neuropsychologist in s5b, submitted once in the training institute's portal for this intern; any change by the intern or the neuropsychologist needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: A drafting step turns the neuropsychologist's outline and the department's protocols into slides and a handout, each statement citing its source, with case examples free of patient identifiers. Supervision, teaching and feedback stay personal. The intern logs supervision hours in the training institute's portal; the neuropsychologist checks them, writes and approves the evaluation, and submits that version in the portal instead of signing, scanning and mailing paper forms. No software rates the intern.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching material was written from scratch and training forms went on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from cited protocols and training portals with hour logs.
tasks.still_hard: Interns who struggle and need more than the standard hours.
tasks.human_edge: Showing an intern how to put a patient at ease during testing.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and paperwork; supervising stays.

evidence.claim: The psychologist stays accountable for AI-drafted text.
Training institutes run portals where interns log supervision hours.

assumptions: Boundary: educating and supervising; educating patients and families (task 22204) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s5b: the hours log entered by the intern in s4 (share 1); the intern's time is about what a paper form took.
Supervising, feedback and evaluation keep their full time.
research_questions: Is preparation for staff training shorter?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist keeps the list of protocols for drafting current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few training sessions, with drafts that need heavy rework (s1 keeps 90), and an institute that still wants signed paper forms (s6 keeps 70) (3.7); high: regular staff training and portal submission (10.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather test findings and referral goals, design the rehabilitation plan, discuss goals with the patient and family, write and approve the plan, share it, and implement it with therapists.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist gathers the test profile, referral goals and therapist notes
Neuropsychologist designs the rehabilitation plan: goals, compensation strategies and exercises for the cognitive dysfunction
Neuropsychologist discusses the proposed goals with the patient and family
Neuropsychologist writes the plan document

loop.input: The neuropsychologist's spoken plan choices, the agreed goals and the test profile in the record.
loop.output: A draft plan in the record's template: goals, strategies, exercises, frequency and review date.
loop.check: Every goal must link to a test finding or a referral question; the neuropsychologist reads each goal against the finding it links to and what the patient agreed, and rewrites anything that does not match.
loop.stop: The neuropsychologist approves the plan, or writes it by hand when the draft is poor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each patient's goals and wording differ.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist checks the final plan: goals against the findings and what the patient agreed, and the patient and therapists it goes to
Neuropsychologist shares the approved plan with the patient and the treating therapists
Neuropsychologist implements the plan: sets up exercises and coordinates with therapists

approvals.approved_version: The plan document as approved by the neuropsychologist in s5, shared with the patient and the therapists named in the record; any edit needs a new approval before sharing.

tasks.design: The patient record shows the test profile, referral goals and therapist notes on one page. Designing the plan and agreeing goals with the patient stay with the neuropsychologist. A speech-to-note step drafts the plan document from the neuropsychologist's spoken choices, and every goal must link to a test finding or referral question. The approved version is shared through the patient portal and with the therapists in the record, instead of printing and mailing it. Setting up exercises and coordinating stay personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were typed from scratch and mailed to therapists.
tasks.still_hard: Patients with little insight into their own deficits.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing goals the patient cares about enough to practise.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; designing and agreeing stay.

reach.learn: Whether therapists start with the plan sooner.

evidence.claim: 24 of 25 large Dutch mental health providers use speech-driven reporting.
Test results and session notes are health data.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and implementing rehabilitation plans; conducting evaluations (task 22193), setting baselines (task 22201) and counselling families (task 22204) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: test profiles from task 22193 and therapist notes stored in the patient record.
Designing, discussing, approving and implementing keep their full time. s4 keeps 75 because the neuropsychologist still dictates the content and corrects the draft.
unknowns: Share of patients using the portal.
research_questions: Do therapists start treatment sooner after the plan?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist keeps the plan template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex plans with many corrections (s4 keeps 90) and therapist notes not in the record (s1 keeps 80) (5.5); high: standard plans drafted well (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
